items.note: S2.1.1 says a fixed linear network exchanges two banks with signs and restores auxiliary values, which is right, but it gives none of the content: h=100, triple-indexed banks, the eight-row copy/gather/scatter/side-injection schedule, or the map (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a).

S2.1.2 states that invertible frames make intermediate frames cancel so that a route applies only an endpoint operator. It omits the edge operator D_vD_u^{-1}, the reason (a common frame commutes with a pointwise linear gate), the explicit endpoint operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, and the fact that sources and sinks also carry frames.

S2.1.3 mentions nested subspaces of an m-dimensional space built from three-element subsets, but gives no budget Wm-2N+2L, no L=Ich, no statement that only the central 3->4 edges decrease (losing h), and no L/N<1/2.

Only alluded to: S2.1.2 says the endpoint operator can be 'an address shear' and S2.1.3 says s<Wm. Missing are the projection matrices, -P_{U_a} at sources, the endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
No step concerns phase frames C_U, translation kernels aI+bX_v, s_c, or C^{tensor m} on every role. S2.2 only lists generic network pages under relies-on.

The plan states s<Wm and that the factor s/W<m gives cost O(Vu^tau) with tau<1. It never gives the cause L<N/2, the deficits eta, the bound s/W<m^tau, or tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, and it does not separate the bit and complex networks.

The cyclic row split among W roles (S2.1.1) and 'in tape order' (S2.1.5) allude to the elementary stream operations and controlled shifts. S2.1 lists stream-operations under relies-on, but no step states the O(V) operations or the controlled-shift lemma.

S2.1.5 gives A=E_1 Pi E_2 with lower triangular factors and a partial permutation with a ones, so a rank-a shear needs a interchanges. It omits that E_1 and E_2 are invertible, the fixed prime q, the O(V) further work, and the one-interchange identity for each one of Pi. It has no method or sub-steps.

Like the paper's proof, the sibling steps go row split into W roles, then frames, then a network with s<Wm, then each edge done by recursive interchanges, then s calls on volume V/W. S2.1.6 omits the hypothesis that the row field is divisible by W^k. The recurrence is given in words, without its O(1) overhead. The route is missing the endpoint identity giving H<-H+D on every role, the conversion of the shear into an interchange (D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D), and the O(V) fixed-tape schedule.

S2.1's statement matches Lemma lem:chunk-swap. Its sub-steps reach only the power-width case (S2.1.6). The paper's reduction to that case is missing: rows taken from rho=O(log e) high digits, padding the rows to a multiple of W^k, base-m pieces, and padding binary ranges to [q^e].
No step mentions binary changes of basis P_M, kernels on coordinate slots, s_c child calls of C^{tensor f}, or recovering H_0 from C.
No step concerns packed selected-bit XORs, whole-chunk cyclic shifts, the bad set, or the repair by sorting.

S2.2 relies on recursive-saving, and S2.1.4's generic 's calls at parameter f on volume V/W' alludes to it. The layer recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the leaves for e<d^beta, the row index from q_0 chunks, and the exponent lambda' are absent.

S2.2 states that H_0 at one bit position in each of at most d chunks costs O(Vd^{lambda'}) with error below sqrt2 2^{-p}, which agrees with the proposition's conclusion. Its hypotheses (K=floor(d^c), the record format, exact evaluation with guard bits before a single truncation) are not given, and it is not derived.

S3.1 correctly gives character cancellation and F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I. S3.2 says only 'at the stated cost': no cost formula, no layout permutation L, no bit-reversed order B, no exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, no error bound. It also calls the transform d-axis when the paper's has d-1 axes.

S3.3 gives signed packing (Kronecker substitution) with the established O(n log n) multiplier, exact numerators, and time O(rp log(rp)), as in the lemma. It omits B_0=2^{4p}, the four products, the centered residues and the output Q_p(fg/r).

S3.4 gives the construction (two forward transforms in the retained layout, pointwise ring products, opposite transform), matching line 3415. It omits the normalization (f*g)/(rM) with the final exact scale by M, the reason P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), and the error and cost bounds.

S4.1 says prime-length transforms are expressed through power-of-two tensor transforms by contractions, with the permutations retained. Missing are the identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, its tensor form, the condition theta>p/alpha^4, and the costs.

S4.2 names Bluestein's identity turning QF_t into a normalized cyclic convolution, but gives neither the chirp a nor the formula. The cancellation of the source permutation R across the forward transforms, product and opposite transform appears in no step.

Only kappa=2^{-182} and the existence of 'fixed rational parameters', p, d and r are mentioned. The parameter values, the sizes (Tp=Theta(n), b, p=6b), and the choice of prime source lengths are absent.
S5 names a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution onto distinct prime axes, but gives neither Phi: x -> prod x_i^{mu_i} nor its triangular mixed-radix form.
S6 repeats the introduction's description without the map x_d -> zeta y with zeta=e^{pi i/r} or the identity M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T.

S7 lists the stages by name (digits, address map, three transforms, scalings, rounding, carries). It omits the source-transform composition (A, chirp transform, B_0, 2^gamma), the opposite transform obtained by conjugation, the pointwise product, and the scales S and 2^{2b+4}S.

S8 states the decisive inequality (error strictly below 1/2, so rounding and carries give the exact product) but none of the quantities that give it: E_s, E_w, the bound 448b 2^{-b+gamma}<=448b 2^{-3b/4}, gamma<=b/4, p=6b.

S9 correctly says every cost-table power is at most 1-2kappa and the total is O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). It omits Tp=Theta(n), the cost-table terms, the margin min g_i=g_2=epsilon c(1-tau), the absorption of log factors into p^kappa, and the schoolbook cutoff.
S0 lists nlogn-conjecture among its relies-on pages, but no step says how the bound refutes an eventual c n lg n lower bound.

errors.says: On a retained layout, parallel butterfly layers and address interchanges compute a d-axis synthetic transform.
errors.paper: The synthetic transform runs over the first d-1 axes, t_i for 1<=i<=d-1 with M=prod_{i<d} t_i. The d-th axis becomes the polynomial coefficient index modulo y^r+1, and M_r convolves only the first d-1 axes over R.

errors.says: Prime-length transforms reduce to power-of-two d-axis transforms of precision p followed by a normalized cyclic convolution.
errors.paper: The source transform is A, then the middle factor QF_t, then B_0, then 2^gamma. The middle power-of-two transform, with its target permutation, is itself converted into a normalized cyclic convolution by Bluestein's chirp identity; the convolution does not follow the transforms.

errors.says: (motivation) a network of linear combinations whose gates need fewer smaller calls than Wm
errors.paper: Gates are pointwise and need no calls. The smaller calls come from edges: each edge costs the rank of its frame difference, and s sums these over edges.

chain: At the top level the tree follows the paper's route: radix digits, CRT, resampling, chirp, twist, synthetic convolution, the two fast procedures, exact recovery and cost accounting. Below the top level most steps are one-line restatements without their formulas. The central saving thins out: the network, labels, dimension budget and endpoint identity are only named, the step from s<Wm to tau=1-2^{-50} is absent, and the shear-to-interchange conversion and the arbitrary-width reduction are missing. The whole numerical side (phase interface, phase-frame recursion, packed selected-bit addition, layer recurrence) is reduced to the bare statement S2.2.

steps.note: A fixed linear network exchanging two banks with signs and restoring auxiliary values is named. h=100, triple-indexed banks, N, m=h^3 and the map (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) are absent.

S2.1.2 says the intermediate frames cancel, leaving an endpoint operator. The mechanism (a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate), D_out S D_in^{-1}, and per-edge cost as a change of frame are not given.

Nested subspaces of an m-dimensional space built from three-element subsets are named. Nondegeneracy in F^{tensor 3} and the fact that only the central 3->4 edges decrease, each losing h, are missing.
S2.1.3 only implies that the subspaces determine the number of calls. It never says rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, nor that the N source edges are rank-one exceptions.
No step gives the budget Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich, or s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
The conclusion s<Wm is stated, but not its cause: L/N=100/539 or 101/539 <1/2, giving the deficit N-2L>0.
S2.1.2 says the endpoint operator can be 'an address shear'. The identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, which makes the shear H<-H+D the same on every role, is absent.
S2.1.5 gives A=E_1 Pi E_2 with a ones in Pi, so a rank-a shear needs a interchanges, and S2.1.4 says a node makes s smaller calls. The O(V) extra work is left implicit.
S2.1.4 describes s calls on volume V/W, with normalized cost growing by s/W<m and giving tau<1. It omits the recurrence's O(1) term, s/W<m^tau, and tau=1-2^{-50} from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs only C8 (edges as recursive calls via the lower-triangular factorization). The fixed network, frames, labels, rank-dimension correspondence, strict saving, endpoint identity and exponent are named without their defining content, and the dimension budget is absent. A reader learns that s<Wm gives a power saving, but not why s<Wm holds or what tau is.
